newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Disetronic acquires Micro Med of U.S.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Disetronic acquires Micro Med of U.S.

text.p: Disetronic Holding AG, a Swiss maker of medical equipment, said it had acquired all of the share capital of Micro Med Inc. of Portsmouth, New Hampshire, for an undisclosed price.
Disetronic said Micro Med was a fast-growing maker of high-quality sterile infusion sets and other sterile medical products.

The purchase will be financed by drawing on part of Disetronic's public offering last year. The final price will depend on Micro Med meeting various financial and production targets over the next three years, a Disetronic statement said.
The two former owners of Micro Med, Dwight Allison and John Riley, retain their management duties, it added.
Micro Med had 1996 sales of $6.13 million and from 1993 to 1996 sales grew at a compound annual rate of some 20 percent. It has about 160 employees.

Disetronic said that it would hold a news conference on May 27 to present 1996/1997 results. In the 1995/96 financial year, which ended March 31, net profit rose 72.1 percent to 13 million Swiss francs and sales rose 23.3 percent to 82.6 million.
Disetronic said sales at Micro Med in its 1997/98 financial year are expected to rise to more than $seven million.
